scientific_queries.note: Four-predictor attribution test on GDSC: annotation ridge, drug marginals, two-way additive, combo lookup.

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round delivers a decisive negative on the programme's own model and rewrites the synthesis promotion verdict to 'nothing to promote'.

design.holdout: 20% of drugs; both settings share the same training rows so only the scoring rule differs

leakage_flag: the 39.25% combo-lookup result in the seen setting is NOT a fair baseline: every combination in that pool appears in training under other cells (combo_seen = 1.00), so lookup is memorisation across the key-level split, exactly the issue R43 raised
clean_result: in the unseen pool no combination appears in training (combo_seen = 0.00), and there the two-way additive model reaches 15.88% against the annotation ridge's 5.75%, a 10.12 pp gap
consistency_with_prior: C19 already measured the additive model at rho = 0.941 on unseen combinations; this round shows the same additive structure also wins at the decision level
consequence: the annotation model has no setting in which it is identified as better; the synthesis promotion verdict changed from 'A promotable but not ours' to 'nothing is worth promoting'
limits: the seen-setting comparison is contaminated by key-level repetition and is reported only as a reference
the additive baseline still requires the cell to appear in training, so it is not a cold-start-cell baseline
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI
next_gates: run the same four-predictor comparison under a joint cell+drug holdout, where the additive model loses its cell marginals
